reading.body:
Troy Balderson's AI record is mostly money: 11 of 17 dated events are contributions from AI and technology company political committees, and every one of them is a donation to him, not a vote he cast against their interest.

The pattern is steady rather than dramatic. Amazon's PAC gave three times across 2025 and 2026, Google's twice, Intel's twice, Meta's twice, with Anthropic, Oracle and a Meta refund filling out the rest. Individual amounts run from $1,000 to $5,000. The contributions arrive in a continuous stream through the period, which is what routine incumbent fundraising from an industry looks like, not a spike around a single bill.

The four recorded votes are all Yea on motions to suspend the rules, a procedure reserved for uncontroversial legislation. The data does not say what H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770 or S. 146 contain, so no link can be drawn between any contribution and any vote. The dates are placed in order for reading, and the ordering is not evidence of cause.

What this does not cover is the substance. There is no record here of committee assignments, sponsored AI bills, floor statements, or positions on data centers, power procurement or grid policy, which is where compute constraints would actually surface in legislation. The money is from AI-adjacent companies, but the votes are on unnamed bills. A reader can see who funds this member and that he votes yes on consensus measures, and nothing more than that.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Troy Balderson: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 17 events.
